title: Integration Contract
description: One entry in the Integration Contract Registry. Describes exactly how the middleware talks to one external system (an ERP, or a commerce store): which entities, in which directions, on what cadence, with what auth, and how failures are handled. In ERP↔store middleware this contract IS the product. It is drafted at G1.5, formalized from Discovery/kickoff mappings, and CLIENT-APPROVED at G-Contracts before any integration code is written. Structural only — do not invent external-API specifics (rate limits, endpoints) we have not verified; leave them null and flag at Discovery.

system.description: Canonical system key matching project.integration_targets (without the 'erp:' prefix is acceptable here). Examples: 'ddi-inform', 'bigcommerce', 'shopify', 'netsuite'.

role.description: What this system is in the data flow. The ERP is typically 'system-of-record' (authoritative for items/inventory/pricing); the store is 'commerce' (authoritative for orders/customers).

directions.description: 'pull' = middleware reads FROM this system. 'push' = middleware writes TO this system. Two-way contracts list both and must define conflict_resolution in 'sync'.

entities.description: Which business entities this contract covers.

type.description: Auth mechanism. 'unknown' is valid pre-Discovery — flag it. DDI Inform access is often partner/credential-gated; verify.

credential_location.description: Where secrets live, e.g. 'env: DDI_API_TOKEN' or a secret-manager ref. Never inline the secret value.

token_refresh.description: How tokens are refreshed/rotated, if applicable (a known failure mode — token expiry).

base_url.description: API base URL. Null/unverified is acceptable pre-Discovery.

api_version.description: Pinned API version, e.g. BigCommerce 'v3'. Enforced by architecture fitness tests.

rate_limits.description: Documented rate limits. Null if unverified — do NOT invent.

max_retries.description: Cap on retries per request. Enforced by architecture fitness tests (queue retry caps).

dead_letter.description: Whether exhausted retries go to a DLQ for webhook-replay/queue-recovery runbooks.

idempotency_key.description: Field/strategy used to dedupe pushes and process webhooks exactly once (e.g. 'X-Idempotency-Key' header, or '{entity}:{external_id}:{updated_at}'). Guards the 'duplicate webhook processed' failure mode.

sync.description: How and when data moves. ERP/CRM default is continuous cron-scheduled sync; webhooks only where the source supports them (store side).

pattern.description: 'scheduled' = cron pull/push (ERP default). 'webhook' = push-from-source (store side). 'polling' = interval poll.

cron.description: Cron expression for 'scheduled'/'polling' (5-field). Interpreted in timezone_source, NOT server-local. e.g. '0 2 * * *' = nightly at the client's 2am.

timezone_source.description: Where the cron's timezone comes from. Always the Dashboard Settings → Timezone / project.timezone, never the server's local tz.

cadence_per_entity.description: Optional per-entity override of the cadence (e.g. inventory every 15 min, items nightly).

incremental.description: True if subsequent runs sync incrementally from a watermark (first run = full sync). Resumable on kill — see watermark-resume tests.

watermark_field.description: Field used as the incremental watermark, e.g. 'modified_at'. Guards the 'sync watermark gap' failure mode.

conflict_resolution.description: Required when directions includes both pull and push. e.g. 'system-of-record wins', 'last-write-wins by updated_at', 'manual review queue'.

overlap_policy.description: A slow run must not stack on the next tick (overlapping-run protection).

field_mapping_ref.description: Path to the detailed field-mapping table (e.g. 'integration-contracts/ddi-inform.fields.md'), the row-by-row 'ERP field → store field' mapping the client signs off on at G-Contracts.

owner.description: Internal owner of this contract (role/email), e.g. 'backend_lead'.

deprecation_date.description: If this contract/API version is sunsetting, the date by which it must be replaced.

failure_modes.description: In-scope failure modes for this system and how each is handled (the pre-flight rule: list before writing integration code).

handling.description: How the middleware handles this mode.

status.description: 'draft' until G-Contracts. No integration code may be written against a 'draft' contract.

approved_by.description: Set at G-Contracts. The internal approver (PM); client approval evidence referenced in the gate notes.
